goal: [MUST] Make public `sennel flow` help a projection of the established parser contract. [MUST] Require every one of the 65 shared routed leaves to expose the same positional, rest, flag, required-value, optional-value, alias, placeholder, description, and implicit -h/--help contract in parsing and leaf help. [MUST] Require flow group help, help flow group, and a group invocation without a leaf to render the same complete child-derived option intersection. [MUST] Require every subcommand row to use at least two ASCII spaces and locale-independent ascending name order. [MUST] Use real CLI probes to cover valid input, defined rejection categories, target guards, runtime and log paths, state-dependent paths, hooks, and exit codes. [MUST] Preserve flow query separately with its stdin, request-file, help, and error behavior. [MUST] Do not merge query into the shared parser. [MUST] Preserve command execution semantics. [MUST] Do not add a command-name limit.

analysis.problem: The public flow help contract is maintained separately from parser declarations, so accepted options, displayed options, group intersections, row spacing, and row order can diverge. Users therefore cannot reliably discover valid invocations, while flow query has a separate parser contract that must remain independent.
analysis.proposedApproach: Use the existing flow command registry and command-definition authority to represent parser-owned options and subcommand rows once, render every shared help entry point from that authority, and derive group options from all direct child leaves. Preserve existing validation, lifecycle, runtime, exit, and query behavior while making the retained public contracts explicit.
analysis.validation: Validation uses a fixed behavior matrix. A meaningful rejection is one real CLI invocation containing exactly one boundary violation from the retained contract: unknown option, repeated singleton flag, missing required value, option-like required value, excess positional or rest input, invalid enum, invalid numeric/ID/path/JSON/ISO/digest value, target-binding mismatch, or a state/config/runtime precondition rejection. A rejection passes only when the established command owner returns its existing non-zero status and diagnostic, no command hook or internal operation runs, and the documented rejection lifecycle, state, runtime directory, and log cleanup remain unchanged. A valid probe passes only when the established zero/non-zero status, output, state transition, artifacts, hooks, runtime path, and log precedence match the retained behavior. The matrix enumerates all 65 shared leaves from FLOW_COMMANDS, compares parser acceptance with leaf help including implicit help, checks every group render entry point, checks short/13/14/15/longest and synthetic 64/65-character row names, and separately checks flow query from stdin, request file, help, and malformed input.

[MUST] Verification uses the real dispatcher or CLI path, enumerates every routed leaf including resume and prepare, covers shared registry consumers, and records observable output, status, state, artifact, hook, runtime, and side-effect results rather than relying on metadata snapshots.
decisionPoints: [MUST] Extend the existing CommandDefinition and FLOW_COMMANDS authority; do not add a parallel command registry. Acceptance is that each listed leaf has one registry-owned parser/help contract consumed by both dispatch and rendering.

[MUST] Own canonical option and row representations at the registry boundary. Acceptance is that parser acceptance, usage, leaf options, and group projections are derived from the same option values and preserve kind, alias, placeholder, description, and requiredness distinctions.

[MUST] Use one shared row renderer for every retained flow group help entry point. Acceptance is byte-equivalent row ordering and separator rules for flow group help, help flow group, and no-leaf group invocation, including the stated length-boundary fixtures.

[MUST] Exclude the query parser from shared option projection, shared admission coverage, and exhaustive shared parser matrices while retaining independent stdin, request-file, help, and error regression checks.

[MUST] Define a rejection fixture as exactly one invalid boundary condition from the analysis.validation list. Exhaustive parser probes check each option and implicit help; focused CLI probes execute valid resume/prepare/abort and guarded get/set/run paths, then assert existing status, diagnostic, state, hooks, runtime, logs, artifacts, and cleanup. A test passes only on the stated observable result, not on registration or mock routing alone.
resolvedByProjectRules: [MUST] Use only Node.js built-in modules because external dependencies are prohibited by project policy.

[MUST] Represent option, row, and rendered-fragment constraints with dedicated classes. OptionContract's constructor requires a non-empty canonical option name, unique aliases, exactly one kind from flag/required-value/optional-value, a non-empty placeholder whenever a value is accepted, and a non-empty description; it rejects duplicate spellings and impossible flag/value combinations. CommandRow's constructor requires a non-empty name and description without line breaks; its renderer emits the name, at least two ASCII spaces, and the description, and its ordering comparator is locale-independent ascending name with a deterministic tie rule. RenderedFragment's constructor accepts only a complete row or option projection plus its explicit render metadata, and toMarkdown() returns the exact stored fragment without adding command-specific policy.
[MUST] Reuse existing APIs and validators before adding abstractions; repeated parser, help, ordering, and rendering decisions belong in the existing command-registry responsibility.
[MUST] Keep execution agent-independent and do not rely on Codex hooks, Claude hooks, IDE lifecycle callbacks, or other host-specific APIs.
[MUST] Preserve command behavior and compatibility; no intentional removal or semantic change is made without an explicit migration decision, and this scope contains none.
[MUST] Keep one bounded specification with measurable requirements and explicit impact on retained public behavior.

[MUST NOT] Change command execution semantics, target guard evaluation, runtime directory policy, rejection lifecycle, or query stdin and request-file behavior.

impactOnExisting: [MUST] User-facing commands affected: `sennel flow` leaf help for all 65 shared leaves; flow group help; `sennel help flow <group>`; group invocation without a leaf; and the independent flow query help/error surface. Command-specific prose and examples remain available.

[MUST] Registry and API contracts affected: FLOW_COMMANDS, existing CommandDefinition option declarations, parser usage generation, leaf help generation, group option intersection, and shared subcommand-row rendering. The registry remains the sole owner and non-Flow registry consumers retain their established semantics.

[MUST] Hooks and configuration affected: existing pre, post, onError, and finally hooks; target binding and guard options; both --agent-work-dir syntaxes; runtime directory resolution; configured log-path precedence; and durable cleanup. No hook order or configuration meaning changes.

[MUST] Generated and persisted artifacts affected: public help text and its row/option projections change; flow state, rejection evidence, runtime logs, configured log files, and command-produced artifacts retain their existing schemas, paths, lifecycle, and cleanup behavior.

[MUST] Side effects affected: valid commands still perform the same internal operation and lifecycle transition, while rejected commands still return the existing diagnostic/status and do not perform a command operation; hooks, state writes, runtime directories, logs, and cleanup are asserted at behavior level.

[MUST] Compatibility expectation: query remains a separate parser contract, no command is intentionally removed, no production name limit is introduced, and every retained public surface has at least one real dispatcher/CLI parity check.
